string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People\'s Republic of China and an important political, cultural, and scientific centre. Its recorded history stretches back more than 3,000 years, and it served as the capital of several major dynasties, including the Yuan, Ming, and Qing. The city combines historic landmarks, such as the Forbidden City and the Great Wall in the surrounding region, with modern universities, research institutions, transport networks, and business districts. Beijing is also known for traditional courtyard houses, Peking opera, and local dishes such as Peking duck.

Shanghai is a major international city on China\'s eastern coast, near the mouth of the Yangtze River. It is a municipality directly under the central government and an important centre for finance, trade, shipping, and innovation. Shanghai developed from a smaller settlement into a major port, particularly after it opened to international trade in 1843. Today, its skyline includes famous landmarks such as the Oriental Pearl Tower and the skyscrapers of Lujiazui. The city also preserves historic neighbourhoods, traditional gardens, and distinctive local food, combining its cultural heritage with a modern urban lifestyle.

Chongqing is a major municipality in southwestern China, located where the Yangtze and Jialing rivers meet. Its mountainous landscape, winding roads, bridges, and rivers give the city a distinctive appearance. Chongqing is an important centre for manufacturing, transportation, logistics, and trade in western China. It also has a rich cultural identity shaped by its history and its location along the Yangtze River. The city is especially famous for Chongqing hot pot, a spicy local dish enjoyed by residents and visitors. Its urban scenery, historic sites, and nearby natural attractions make it an important destination.

Tianjin is a municipality in northern China near the Bohai Sea, southeast of Beijing. The Haihe River flows through the city, which has long served as an important port and transport hub. Tianjin officially became a city in 1404 and later developed into a major centre for industry, commerce, finance, and education. Its history is reflected in a variety of architectural styles, including traditional Chinese buildings and European-style structures in historic districts. Today, Tianjin combines a busy port, modern industrial areas, universities, and cultural attractions. Local specialities, including Goubuli steamed buns, are also part of its identity.
